The tally clerk issues work assignments. Until one is appointed, issue them yourself. Any assignment can be changed.
{crop}: not enough seed for {hectares} {hectares}|plural(one=hectare,other=hectares). We will sow less.
{person_family} was calm when I was appointed. He knows my village on paper, but not on the ground. Let's see how he handles something the papers don't show.
{person_family} looked at me without fuss. I met managers like that at the factory: they want progress, not promises. I'll show him results when there's something to show.
When I was appointed, I kept thinking I ought to say something sensible. The secretary looked calm, which only made me more nervous. I don't yet know what he thinks of me.
{person_family} signed a new order. I don't believe he knows nothing about my previous farm. This time, I'd better give him a reason to talk about the work here.
The order bears a signature: {person_family}. When we met, he gave no sign that my family connection at the regional committee made any difference to him. Better rely on my own results.
{person_family} was calm, and I watched closely. I don't like chiefs who substitute noise for work. He doesn't seem that sort. For now, he's given me a post; respect still has to be earned.
{person_address} saves words as some men save money. He watched closely when I was appointed. I'd like to know exactly what he noticed.
{person_family} signed the order calmly, without any grand promises. Not the first time I've started work like that. Too early to judge him; I'll see how he treats work that's actually done.

At the church, {person_address} wore the same frock coat I remember from childhood. Still makes himself presentable when he meets people. He knows this land, but deciding for the village is my job now.
{person_family} stood by the church in his best frock coat. Clothes don't tell you how a man works. When we talk business, I'll learn what he relies on here.
At the church, {person_address} was dressed more formally than I expected. I'd meant to ask him about the village, but now I don't know where to begin. The road, perhaps. I've seen that already.
{person_family} put on his frock coat to greet the new chairman. I noticed the respect, but I don't judge a man by his clothes. He'll tell me more about local affairs when we meet at work.
{person_family} came to the welcome in a frock coat. Proper procedure observed. He was calm, not trying to please. Better talk to him about places and people than my appointment.
{person_family} stood by the church in a frock coat, as if on parade. Calm. I noticed that. I'll ask what he knows of the farm, without parade-ground speeches.
I noticed the distinctive frock coat at once. {person_address} greeted me by the church without fuss. A coat alone won't tell you a man's worth; talk of the farm will show it.
{person_family} put on a frock coat for my arrival. So he thought the welcome mattered. Once work begins, I'll see what he knows about the people and the land.
{person_family} signed my appointment order. My village is my responsibility now.
{person_address} was among those welcoming me on arrival. We haven't discussed the village layout yet.
{person_family} signed the order. The factory is behind me; this farm is my responsibility now.
{person_family} wore a frock coat at the church. Before taking his advice, I'll ask him about the work.
{person_family} signed the appointment order. Now my calculations will have to stand the test of a real farm.
{person_address} wore a frock coat at the church. I wanted to ask about the village, but we haven't talked yet.
{person_family} signed a new order. After my dismissal, I've been given a second chance.
{person_family} wore a frock coat at the church. We haven't discussed the farm; first I'll check his words against the place.
{person_family} signed the order. I have the appointment; now I'll be held to account for results.
{person_family} wore a frock coat at the church. The welcome is over; a working conversation still lies ahead.
{person_family} signed the order. The people here are my responsibility now.
{person_family} wore a frock coat at the church. I'll return to the business at hand when I leave the office.
{person_family} signed the order. Paper gave me the post; the farm still has to be put back on its feet.
I noticed an old frock coat by the church. {person_family} was wearing it. I'll know him now; we'll discuss the farm separately.
{person_family} signed the order. Once again, I'm responsible for the work, whatever the post is called.
{person_family} stood by the church in a frock coat. A memorable welcome; I'll ask about the people and places at work.
